subject: SIG request — code gate trace & CI secrets stewardship
messages:
From: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@northbridge-assessors.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SIG intake — request for secure development artifacts

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks for the quick onboarding call last week. As part of the SIG review we need a compact bundle of artifacts demonstrating Redwood's secure development controls focusing on: code review gate evidence, CI/CD runner secrets handling, and change-management approvals for production deploys during Q4 2026 — specifically any artefacts that show provenance (PR -> CI -> deploy) and who had privileged access to secrets at run time.

Can you provide: 1) an export showing PR approvals and merge gate policy for the last 30 PRs to the inference runtime repo, 2) a diagram or doc describing how ephemeral secrets are issued to CI runners and rotated, and 3) change log entries showing approvals for at least two production rollouts (can be redacted).

A single zip with a short README is ideal. We need this by end of day Thursday PST to stay on schedule.

Best,
Diane
Diane Kerr
Security Assessments | NorthBridge Assessors

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Diane Kerr <diane.kerr@northbridge-assessors.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SIG intake — request for secure development artifacts

Diane —

Thanks for the clear list. We'll assemble a package and include a short README explaining what is redacted and why. Monica will lead collection for PR/merge evidence; Grace will add the CI secrets flow and the runner IAM role docs; I'll pull the change-log exports and annotate the approval trail.

One ask: for the PR export do you need raw GitHub audit events or is a CSV of PR numbers + approver names + timestamps sufficient? The CSV is quicker to produce.

We aim to deliver a zip to your SFTP by EoD Thursday PST.

— Vanessa
Vanessa Ortiz
Director, GtM Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference

Hi Diane —

Attaching two items: 1) a short explainer PDF (ci-runner-iam-roles.pdf) that documents how ephemeral IAM roles are provisioned via our runner-controller and how tokens are minted per-job with a TTL of 15 minutes, and 2) a diagram link in the README showing the flow: PR->CI->artifact-store->staging-deploy->canary->prod. Important controls called out: ephemeral secrets, workload-scoped roles (no static long-lived service account keys), and automated rotation of runner tokens.

Also included in the README: the policy that forbids storing plaintext secrets in repos (pre-commit hook + server-side secret-scan), with sample enforcement logs.

Grace

Subject: Re: SIG intake — request for secure development artifacts — package delivered

Diane —

We uploaded a zip to your SFTP and also placed a human-readable README in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/NDG-432-sig-artifacts. The zip contains: pr-review-export_2027-02-20.csv, ci-runner-iam-roles.pdf, change-log-2027-02-21.txt, and a README.md that explains the redactions and references JIRA SECOPS-1183 for the rollback investigation.

Summary of controls called out in README:
- Mandatory 2-approver rule for high-risk repositories; PR gating enforced by branch protection and CI status checks.
- Ephemeral secrets: runner controller issues short-lived tokens per job; tokens TTL = 15m; no long-lived keys in runners.
- Secret scanning and pre-commit hooks block commits; server-side scans prevent merges with high-confidence matches.
- Change management: deploys require release manager + eng manager approval; automated canary with rollback hooks.

If you need deeper raw audit logs we can discuss an NDAs' addendum. Happy to hop on a quick call to walk through the artifacts.

— Vanessa
Director, GtM Security & Compliance | Redwood Inference
